statements.__comment: CIDR blocks (vpc.py labels them AWSCidrBlock) of the VPCs statement 3 treats as this account's, so a VPC it deletes leaves no orphan blocks. Blocks of another account's VPC (arn names that account) and of peer stubs reached only through a peering (aws_import_vpc_peering_cleanup.json) are left alone.
statements.query: MATCH (n:AWSCidrBlock)<-[:BLOCK_ASSOCIATION]-(v:AWSVpc)<-[:RESOURCE]-(:AWSAccount{id: $AWS_ID})<-[:OWNER]-(:AWSOrganization{id: $ORGANIZATION_ID})<-[:OWNER]-(:CloudanixWorkspace{id: $WORKSPACE_ID}) WHERE n.lastupdated <> $UPDATE_TAG AND coalesce(split(v.arn, ':')[4], $AWS_ID) = $AWS_ID WITH DISTINCT n LIMIT $LIMIT_SIZE DETACH DELETE (n) return COUNT(*) as TotalCompleted

MATCH (:AWSCidrBlock)<-[r:BLOCK_ASSOCIATION]-(v:AWSVpc)<-[:RESOURCE]-(:AWSAccount{id: $AWS_ID})<-[:OWNER]-(:AWSOrganization{id: $ORGANIZATION_ID})<-[:OWNER]-(:CloudanixWorkspace{id: $WORKSPACE_ID}) WHERE r.lastupdated <> $UPDATE_TAG AND coalesce(split(v.arn, ':')[4], $AWS_ID) = $AWS_ID WITH DISTINCT r LIMIT $LIMIT_SIZE DELETE (r) return COUNT(*) as TotalCompleted

statements.__comment: A VPC whose arn names another account is that account's, reached through a legacy peering RESOURCE edge. Leave it; the next statement drops the stale edge. A missing or unparseable arn is deleted as before.
statements.query: MATCH (n:AWSVpc)<-[:RESOURCE]-(:AWSAccount{id: $AWS_ID})<-[:OWNER]-(:AWSOrganization{id: $ORGANIZATION_ID})<-[:OWNER]-(:CloudanixWorkspace{id: $WORKSPACE_ID}) WHERE n.lastupdated <> $UPDATE_TAG AND coalesce(split(n.arn, ':')[4], $AWS_ID) = $AWS_ID WITH n LIMIT $LIMIT_SIZE DETACH DELETE (n) return COUNT(*) as TotalCompleted

MATCH (:AWSVpc)<-[r:RESOURCE]-(:AWSAccount{id: $AWS_ID})<-[:OWNER]-(:AWSOrganization{id: $ORGANIZATION_ID})<-[:OWNER]-(:CloudanixWorkspace{id: $WORKSPACE_ID}) WHERE r.lastupdated <> $UPDATE_TAG WITH r LIMIT $LIMIT_SIZE DELETE (r) return COUNT(*) as TotalCompleted
